machine: Flash (Vinay's Ubuntu box, ssh flash, 12 threads, qwen-test venv: python 3.14 + numpy 2.5.4 + tokenizers 0.23.3)
question: GPT-OSS 120B, fresh-eyes review (results/fresh_perspective.md): why not a plain 1-bit delta at the same bytes, i.e. a baseline against an existing delta codec?

model_pair.matrices: embedding + 24 blocks x (attn.q/k/v/o_proj, mlp.gate/up/down_proj) = 169 delta matrices

probe_set: the same combined 96 fresh held-out questions and the same scoring (mean target logprob, Signet convention, Stage 2 NumPy forward) as results/alien_sweep_heldout96.json

pricing.bitdelta_price_formula: ceil(total_weights / 8) + 4 bytes x n_matrices (one fp32 scale per matrix)

bitdelta_init.definition: BitDelta initialization (Liu et al., arXiv:2402.10193): per matrix, delta_hat = sign(delta) * mean(|delta|); one fp32 scale per matrix; NO scale distillation and NO training. The full BitDelta method distills the scales on data afterwards; that step is deliberately not run, and this config must be cited as the initialization, not as BitDelta's final reported quality.

factored_uniform_rank108.definition: factored.quantize_delta at uniform rank 108 on all 169 matrices: the largest uniform rank whose factored.storage_bytes total fits under the plain 1-bit price.

two_budget_curve.framing: A plain 1-bit delta has a floor price: 1 bit per weight over the 169 matrices plus one scale per matrix. At the 19.4 MB headline budget no plain 1-bit delta fits, so the honest comparison is a curve with two budgets, not one.

budget_19mb_factored_only.plain_1bit_delta: does not fit: floor price is 61745828 bytes

api_calls: none for the measurements (compute only); the Spark judging pass over this file is logged in results/api_usage_log.jsonl
